Added two citations from Lawrence Beesley's day-of survivor account: collision felt as a slight jar with passengers initially unconcerned and card game continuing, followed by muster order; and men ordered away from lifeboats, women boarding quietly, Beesley's exchange with crew to board, and stoker elected lifeboat captain; contemporaneous primary account from already-cited survivor: The Newark Advocate, Apr 19, 1912, via NewspaperArchive

Added three citations from day-of wire report (Apr 19, 1912): primary newspaper source for "Nearer My God to Thee" claim replacing book citation; Carpathia Marconi operator Harold Cotton named and credited with catching Titanic's first distress call; and survivor accounts of life-preserver bodies floating as boats departed; sourced to contemporaneous wire report: The Newark Advocate, Apr 19, 1912, via NewspaperArchive

Added three citations from third-class survivor Gunner Tenglin: Captain Smith personally entering third class to order crew out under threat of fine; collapsible boat B conditions including 150 swimmers reduced to 12 survivors with dead bodies thrown overboard to prevent swamping; and two women jumping from lifeboats on realising those left behind would not be saved; fills three uncited gaps with steerage perspective absent from article: Webster City Freeman, Apr 30, 1912, via NewspaperArchive

Added two citations from survivor Lydia Chaffee's private letter (written days after disaster): false reassurances given to women that husbands would follow in other boats, and boats tipping during lowering causing women to drown; intimate firsthand account fills two uncited gaps in evacuation section: The Quincy Daily Journal, Apr 29, 1912, via NewspaperArchive

Added three citations from the official surviving passengers' committee statement (Apr 19, 1912): Board of Trade lifeboat capacity discrepancy (950 places for 3,500 passengers), survivors' formal call for international lifeboat law predating official inquiries, and collective praise of Carpathia crew; sourced to contemporaneous primary document: The Clermont Courier, Apr 24, 1912, via NewspaperArchive

Expanded Phillips's death from a single word to a named eyewitness account: Thomas Whiteley confirmed Phillips reached collapsible boat B but died before rescuers could revive him, and was one of four buried at sea from Carpathia; replaces uncited "Phillips perished" with contemporaneous wire report: Topeka State Daily Journal, Apr 19, 1912, via NewspaperArchive

Added three Frauenthal survivor quotes: passenger psychology explaining lifeboat reluctance, Astor's last reported words ("Good luck!"), and firsthand explanation for lifeboats not returning for survivors; contemporaneous account fills three uncited gaps: The Sun (New York), May 10, 1912, via NewspaperArchive
